concept.title: Infinite Log-Concavity of Total d-Hoggatt Numbers
concept.concept_description: The sequence of total d-Hoggatt numbers, defined as the row sums H_d(n) = sum_{k=0}^n H_d(n,k), is infinitely log-concave for all d >= 1. The paper proves the infinite log-concavity of the row and column sequences of the d-Hoggatt triangle. However, the infinite log-concavity of the total d-Hoggatt numbers remains open, encompassing the unresolved infinite log-concavity of the Baxter numbers for d=3 and Catalan numbers for d=2.
concept.mathematical_framing: The sequence of total d-Hoggatt numbers, defined as the row sums H_d(n) = sum_{k=0}^n H_d(n,k), is infinitely log-concave for all d >= 1. The paper proves the infinite log-concavity of the row and column sequences of the d-Hoggatt triangle. However, the infinite log-concavity of the total d-Hoggatt numbers remains open, encompassing the unresolved infinite log-concavity of the Baxter numbers for d=3 and Catalan numbers for d=2.
concept.lean_guess: Leverage the real-rootedness of the row generating functions (proven by Dilks and Fang-Zhang-Zhao) combined with the theory of multiplier sequences or Pólya frequency sequences to establish the infinite log-concavity of the total sums. Alternatively, employ recurrence relations and induction with tight asymptotic bounds derived from the asymptotic normality of the row sequences.

concept.title: Sign changes of symmetric power L-function coefficients along sums of squares
concept.concept_description: Conjecture that for any normalized Hecke eigenform f of even weight for SL(2,Z), any integer j ≥ 1, and any even m with 2 ≤ m ≤ 12, the number of sign changes of the j-th symmetric power L-function coefficient λ_sym^j f(n) as n runs over integers representable as a sum of m squares up to x is at least C·x/(log x) for some constant C>0 depending only on f, j, and m.
concept.mathematical_framing: Conjecture that for any normalized Hecke eigenform f of even weight for SL(2,Z), any integer j ≥ 1, and any even m with 2 ≤ m ≤ 12, the number of sign changes of the j-th symmetric power L-function coefficient λ_sym^j f(n) as n runs over integers representable as a sum of m squares up to x is at least C·x/(log x) for some constant C>0 depending only on f, j, and m.
concept.lean_guess: Use an asymptotic formula for the second moment of λ_sym^j f(n) sums of m squares, together with spectral sieve to obtain a power-saving term moment; then apply a Turán-type lemma to obtain a power-saving bound on the variance of λ_sym^j f(n) over sums of m squares via Voronoi summation and Weil bounds for Kloosterman sums. Combine this with a large sieve inequality to improve the bound on the first moment. Finally, apply a Turán-type lemma to translate a nontrivial bound on the first moment into a quantitative lower bound for the number of sign changes.

concept.title: Geometric Bombieri--Lang Conjecture for Varieties Fibered Over Curves with Generic Fiber of General Type
concept.concept_description: Let K/k be a finitely generated extension of characteristic zero, and let f: X → C be a dominant morphism from a smooth projective variety X over K to a smooth projective curve C over k, such that the generic fiber X_η is of general type over the function field K(C) = K. Then, after removing a proper Zariski closed subset S ⊂ X, all K-rational points of X lie in the union of fibered components and constant families parametrized by subvarieties of C. In particular, X(K) ∩ (X \ S) is not Zariski dense in X.
concept.mathematical_framing: Let K/k be a finitely generated extension of characteristic zero, and let f: X → C be a dominant morphism from a smooth projective variety X over K to a smooth projective curve C over k, such that the generic fiber X_η is of general type over the function field K(C) = K. Then, after removing a proper Zariski closed subset S ⊂ X, all K-rational points of X lie in the union of fibered components and constant families parametrized by subvarieties of C. In particular, X(K) ∩ (X \ S) is not Zariski dense in X.
concept.lean_guess: The proof strategy involves three main components: (1) Use the minimal model program to show that a fibration f: X → C with general type generic fiber admits a canonical fibration structure after removing negligible subvarieties; (2) Apply the framework of Vojta's dictionary to construct entire curves on complex conjugates of fibers from rational points of large height; (3) Combine the Xie--Yuan--Gao theorem on varieties admitting finite morphisms to abelian varieties with equidistribution results to show that such constructed entire curves must be contained in proper subvarieties, forcing the rational points to lie in the special loci. Technical tools include potential theory, height machinery, and the arithmetic Simpson correspondence between heights and curvature.
catalog_references: Bombieri, G. 'La question de Mittag-Leffler et les courbes algébriques', 1982
Vojta, P. 'Comparing Roth's inequality and Salberger's inequality', 2001
Faltings, G. 'The proof of the Mordell conjecture', 1986
Xie, G.; Yuan, X. 'On the geometric Bombieri--Lang conjecture over function fields', 2022
Gao, G. 'Rational points and geometric invariant theory', 2023
